chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in the dogs except for the hunting dog, or a herding dog.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (referring to Imam Ali, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of dogs considered beneficial in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), quoting Imam Ali (peace be upon him), establishes the principle of *al-khilqah* (creation/utility) in evaluating dogs, limiting their general permissibility to functional roles like hunting and herding. It reflects the practical realities of 7th-century Arabian society where dogs were primarily working animals, a context that Shia jurists use to derive rulings on keeping dogs for specific needs versus general ownership. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on purpose-driven utility (*maslaha*) in distinguishing between beneficial and less desirable aspects of creation.
